Calculate sum of maximum spectral power for sedimentation rates for a wavelet spectra

Source: R/sum_power_sedrate.R
sum_power_sedrate.Rd

The sum_power_sedrate function is used calculate the sum of maximum spectral power for a list of astronomical cycles from a wavelet spectra. The data is first normalised using the average spectral power curves for a given percentile based on results of the model_red_noise_wt function

Usage

sum_power_sedrate(
  red_noise = NULL,
  wavelet = NULL,
  percentile = NULL,
  sedrate_low = NULL,
  sedrate_high = NULL,
  spacing = NULL,
  cycles = c(NULL),
  x_lab = "depth",
  y_lab = "sedrate",
  run_multicore = FALSE,
  n_cores = NULL,
  genplot = FALSE,
  plot_res = 1,
  keep_editable = FALSE,
  palette_name = "viridis",
  color_brewer = "viridis",
  verbose = FALSE,
  colour_brewer = NULL
)

Arguments

red_noise

Red-noise power curves (required): the output of model_red_noise_wt for the same wavelet, a matrix with one row per period of wavelet and one column per red-noise simulation. Default=NULL.

wavelet

Wavelet object (required) created with analyse_wavelet, of a record with depth in metres. Default=NULL.

percentile

Percentile of the red-noise power (numeric, between 0 and 1) by which the wavelet power is weighted: at every period the threshold is the percentile quantile of a normal distribution with the mean and standard deviation of the red_noise runs. This accounts for the distortion of the power spectrum by the analytical technique and by random red noise. Required. Default=NULL.

sedrate_low

Lowest sedimentation rate tested, in cm/kyr (numeric, > 0). Required. Default=NULL.

sedrate_high

Highest sedimentation rate tested, in cm/kyr (numeric, > sedrate_low). Required. Default=NULL.

spacing

Step between the tested sedimentation rates, in cm/kyr (numeric, > 0). Required. Default=NULL.

cycles

Periods of the astronomical cycles, in kyr (numeric vector, e.g. c(405, 125, 95, 40, 21)), whose expected periods in depth (sedimentation rate x period) are searched for in the scalogram. Required. Default=c(NULL).

x_lab

Label of the depth axis of the plot (character). Default="depth".

y_lab

Label of the sedimentation rate axis of the plot (character). Default="sedrate".

run_multicore

Run the calculation for the positions along the record in parallel on several cores (logical). Default=FALSE.

n_cores

Number of cores used when run_multicore = TRUE (integer, or NULL). NULL uses an automatic, safe number: physical cores minus one, at most 4, and limited by the free memory; set options(waverider.n_cores = ...) to change it. A value > 1 also switches on parallel computing. Results do not depend on the number of cores. Default=NULL.

genplot

Plot the result (selected with plot_res) as a depth versus sedimentation rate map with its average curve (logical). Default=FALSE.

plot_res

Which result to plot when genplot = TRUE (integer): 1 the normalised sum of maximum spectral power, 2 the number of astronomical components found. Default=1.

keep_editable

Keep the graphical parameters of the plot after the function returns, so that extra elements can be added (logical); only used with genplot = TRUE. Default=FALSE.

palette_name

Name of the colour palette of the power (colour) scale, a character string. Which names are valid depends on color_brewer:

  • color_brewer = "grDevices": "rainbow", "heat.colors", "terrain.colors", "topo.colors", "cm.colors", or any of the 115 hcl.colors palettes (list them with grDevices::hcl.pals()), for example "viridis", "Plasma", "Inferno", "YlOrRd", "Spectral", "Blue-Red", "Zissou 1".

  • color_brewer = "viridis": "viridis", "magma", "inferno", "plasma", "cividis", "rocket", "mako", "turbo".

  • color_brewer = "RColorBrewer": "BrBG", "PiYG", "PRGn", "PuOr", "RdBu", "RdGy", "RdYlBu", "RdYlGn", "Spectral", "Accent", "Dark2", "Paired", "Pastel1", "Pastel2", "Set1", "Set2", "Set3", "Blues", "BuGn", "BuPu", "GnBu", "Greens", "Greys", "Oranges", "OrRd", "PuBu", "PuBuGn", "PuRd", "Purples", "RdPu", "Reds", "YlGn", "YlGnBu", "YlOrBr", "YlOrRd" (also listed by wr_brewer_palettes()).

  • color_brewer = "colorRamps": "blue2green", "blue2green2red", "blue2red", "blue2yellow", "cyan2yellow", "green2red", "magenta2green", "matlab.like", "matlab.like2", "ygobb".

  • color_brewer = "scico" (all except "batlowK" need the scico package): "acton", "bam", "bamako", "bamO", "batlow", "batlowK", "batlowW", "berlin", "bilbao", "broc", "brocO", "buda", "bukavu", "cork", "corkO", "davos", "devon", "fes", "glasgow", "grayC", "hawaii", "imola", "lajolla", "lapaz", "lipari", "lisbon", "managua", "navia", "nuuk", "oleron", "oslo", "roma", "romaO", "tofino", "tokyo", "turku", "vanimo", "vik", "vikO".

Low power is drawn with the first colour of the palette and high power with the last. Default="viridis".

color_brewer

Palette family from which palette_name is taken, a character string: "grDevices", "viridis", "RColorBrewer", "colorRamps" or "scico" (the last one, except for "batlowK", needs the scico package). See palette_name for the palette names of each family. Default="viridis".

verbose

Show the progress of the calculation (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=FALSE.

colour_brewer

British spelling of color_brewer, with the same options; if given (not NULL) it overrides color_brewer. Default=NULL.

Value

Returns a list which contains 4 elements element 1: sum of maximum spectral power element 2: number of cycles used in the sum of maximum spectral power element 3: y-axis values of the matrices which is sedimentation rate element 4: x-axis values of the matrices which is depth

If Default="TRUE" a plot is created with 3 subplots. Subplot 1 is plot in which the the sum of maximum spectral power for a given sedimentation rate or nr of cycles is plotted for each depth given depth. Subplot 2 is a plot in which the average sum of maximum spectral power is plotted fro each sedimentation Subplot 3 is a color scale for subplot 1.

Author

Based on the asm and eAsm functions of the 'astrochron' R package and the 'eCOCO' and 'COCO' functions of the 'Acycle' software

Examples

# \donttest{
#estimate sedimentation rate for the the magnetic susceptibility record
# of the Sullivan core of Pas et al., (2018).

mag_wt <- analyse_wavelet(data = mag[1:200, ],
dj = 1/10,
lowerPeriod = 0.1,
upperPeriod = 32,
verbose = FALSE,
omega_nr = 10)

#increase n_simulations to better define the red noise spectral power curve
mag_wt_red_noise <- model_red_noise_wt(wavelet=mag_wt,
n_simulations = 3,
run_multicore=FALSE,
verbose=FALSE)

sedrates <- sum_power_sedrate(red_noise=mag_wt_red_noise,
wavelet=mag_wt,
percentile=0.75,
sedrate_low = 0.5,
sedrate_high = 4,
spacing = 1,
cycles = c(2376,1600,1180,696,406,110),
x_lab="depth",
y_lab="sedrate",
run_multicore=FALSE,
genplot = FALSE,
plot_res=1,
keep_editable=FALSE,
palette_name = "rainbow",
color_brewer="grDevices",
verbose=FALSE)
# }
